Its diff to .beads/issues.jsonl reverted all 17 records that run had written AND DELETED BEAD bd-mhcrc OUTRIGHT. === THE SAME CLASS RECURRED LIVE DURING THIS RUN — TWICE — AND THE RECOVERY IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN ===
Both pushes were rejected (an ac-batch-close session landed 1a1c47bf+41068b1b, then ee56bf4f). `git rebase origin/main` CONFLICTED ON .beads/issues.jsonl. Every reflexive resolution (take-ours, force-push, hand-edit the conflict) is a whole-file overwrite and would have reproduced c64011e6 exactly, this time deleting their bd-acreview-20260804-curate-r0-730as.7. WHAT WORKED, adopt as standard: `git rebase --abort` -> `git checkout --detach origin/main` (take THEIR file verbatim; the local commit stays reachable by sha) -> `br sync` (IMPORT — this direction MERGES correctly) -> `br sync --flush-only` -> then PROVE it with `comm -23 <their tip ids> <result ids>` which must be EMPTY. Round 1: Created 1 / Updated 2 / Skipped 2547. Round 2: Created 1 / Updated 1 / Skipped 2549. Both rounds: zero ids lost, exactly 2 added (my two proposal beads), all 23 label ops retained, their new beads intact.
THIS CHANGES THE FORK SCORING: br sync's IMPORT direction already merges correctly. The defect is entirely in letting the EXPORT direction run from a DB that never imported. So Fork C is not merely 'narrows the window' — it CLOSED it completely here, twice, and is available today at zero cost. C is the cheap mitigation; B is the guard for when someone forgets. Memo updated to say so.
NOTE: dcg blocks `git reset --hard` (core.git:reset-hard). `git checkout --detach origin/main` on a clean tree is the allowed equivalent and is strictly safer — the local commit stays reachable.

=== TOOLING NOTES ===
(1) slack-send still has NO --dry-run (TENTH night). The probe prints 'unrecognized arguments' AND exits 0 — a misleading pair that passes a naive exit-code check. Resolved by reading infrastructure/slack/channels.json; sofi = C0AQ7964ZU6. Heartbeat step 0 should just say to read channels.json.
(2) The jq scoping trap bit AGAIN, exactly as documented last night, and it is worth stating as a rule rather than an anecdote: inside index()/contains() the `.` rebinds to the argument. ALWAYS bind first (`. as $d | select(($epics|index($d.depends_on_id)) != null)`). Unbound, it fails loudly with 'Cannot index array with string' — which is the GOOD case. The field name is `depends_on_id`, NOT `depends_on`; getting THAT wrong returns null silently and produces plausible false results. board-scan.md should name the field explicitly.
(3) `tr` is a tmux alias in the fleet's interactive profile — board-scan.md warns about this and it bit anyway, printing 'open terminal failed: not a terminal' 40 times inside a loop. Use awk/gsub instead of tr in any scanning loop.
(4) `br show <id> --json` returns a bare ARRAY (use `.[0].id`), unlike `br list --json` which returns `{issues:[...]}`. Add this to board-scan.md's shape table — it currently documents only list and ready.
(5) `br comments add` DELIBERATELY NOT USED again (bd-9edhn: per-DB autoincrement comment ids collide across concurrent DBs). Tonight's clobber makes the case stronger, not weaker. The heartbeat should say outright: NIGHTLY must not write bead comments while bd-9edhn is open.
